passage:
An old theater was damaged by fire. Some people wanted to build a modern shopping center in its place. Others wanted to rebuild the theater.
The town debated for months. Finally, they rebuilt the front of the theater and added modern safety systems inside.
When it reopened, the first show was about the theater's own history. Former actors, ticket sellers, and visitors shared memories.
The building was not exactly the same as before, but it carried the past into a safer future.
Preservation does not always mean freezing time. Sometimes it means choosing which parts must remain and which parts must change so a place can live again.
